I was eleven years old. It was the height of the Pokémon card game fad at my school. I finally had enough cards to justify a binder to store them. Excitement ran through me as I went to to local card shop after school. I grabbed the hard cover binder and ten plastic card sheets (9 slots per sheet). $5 for the binder and $0.10 per sheet, not including tax. I handed the cashier my hard earned allowance and then headed home.

So anxious to start organizing my cards, I started to fit my plastic sheets into the binder. To my young horror, I counted not ten, but eleven plastic sheets. ELEVEN!

What was I supposed to do? My mom had already driven me halfway home and had taken time out of her day so we could buy the binder. Would she think I stole it? Would she punish me? So many questions keep pounding my young head.

I kept it. My shame prevented me from doing the right thing, and I kept it. Fifteen year later, it holds my two beautiful 1st edition holographic Charizards. It sits it it's sticker covered glory on my bookshelf as a constant reminder to the pain I caused that store.

I will never forget what I did...
